findings.reason: the section must name the assertion block to remove (the parser lines) rather than a test that does not exist, or the node's own rewrite silently drops coverage of §6's landed prompt and brief.
findings.text: §22 says it deletes "the test that exercised only them", but no test exercised only the parser: the single test that touches `parse_figure_review` is `test_figure_prompt_and_parser_cover_every_visual_rule` (tests/test_figure_review.py:285–315), which also asserts that `reckon/crew/prompts/figure_review.md` names all six `FIGURE_REVIEW_ITEMS`, that the prompt states its read-only and do-not-edit rules, and that the dispatch brief carries the five brief phrases — and it is the only test in the tree pinning those, since `FIGURE_REVIEW_ITEMS` survives §22 as production data (reckon/crew/review.py:277). The done-when's guard clause, "the rest of that file passes unchanged in what it asserts" (plan.html:2684), measures the other five tests and so cannot catch the loss: a worker that deletes the whole function as the sentence tells it leaves every clause satisfied while removing the only regression guard for the figure prompt and brief that §6 landed.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `reckon/crew/review.py`, `tests/test_figure_review.py`, `parse_figure_review` (review.py:944), `_FIGURE_RUBRIC_LINE_RE` (:544), `_PLAN_RUBRIC_LINE_RE` (:1013), `store_review` (:2562) and `read_review` (:3985) all resolve, and §6 did land the parser (`b11687d2c`, `feat(crew): dispatch read-only figure reviews`).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §22 instructs deleting "the test that exercised only them", but no such test exists and the one test that touches the parser also carries §6's prompt and brief coverage, so the done-when's "rest of that file" clause does not protect it.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — write paths are the two source files, and every log is required under the run directory with a revision header and an `EXIT=` tail (plan.html:2684), matching §14–§17.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the section removes symbols rather than adding them, and no plan label, stage name or ticket number appears in its text or in the symbols it names.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the stated root cause matches the evidence: a repo-wide search finds `parse_figure_review` only at its own definition and at one test, so the emitted figure text is parsed by nobody and the record path is `store_review`; the fallback claim also holds, since `FIGURE_REVIEW_ITEMS` (review.py:277) are all `[a-z_]+` and match `_PLAN_RUBRIC_LINE_RE` while a figure-record read is keyed on the `rubric` field (`_review_rubric_matches`, review.py:2196).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — one deliverable, stated once: delete `parse_figure_review` and `_FIGURE_RUBRIC_LINE_RE` because nothing in production calls them (plan.html:2682).
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `plan-section-depends-on` carries `s22: ["scoring-should-stop-a-promotion#s6"]` (plan.html:31), which resolves to the section that landed the parser §22 removes, and §6 is `done`; no other edge is needed and none points at the wrong node.
